summary:
## Project Summary — ASTRA-MED

I developed **ASTRA-MED (Astronaut Health Monitoring & Mission Control System)**, a Python-based desktop application designed to simulate and monitor astronaut health during space missions. The system combines real-time simulated vital-sign monitoring, interactive health analytics, AI-powered anomaly detection, automated alerts, astronaut profiles, mission management, and medical report generation in one centralized platform.

The project addresses the challenge of organizing and interpreting astronaut health data in a demanding space-mission environment. By using simulated telemetry, personalized health baselines, and Isolation Forest machine learning, ASTRA-MED identifies unusual health patterns, highlights potential anomalies, and presents meaningful insights through an intuitive mission-control dashboard.

This project is important because astronaut well-being is essential to mission safety and success. ASTRA-MED demonstrates how software engineering, data visualization, and artificial intelligence can support health-monitoring workflows and contribute to the development of smarter space-health management systems.
details:
ASTRA-MED — Project Details

1. What does the project do and how does it work?

I developed ASTRA-MED (Astronaut Health Monitoring & Mission Control System), a Python-based desktop application designed to simulate and monitor astronaut health during space missions. It provides a centralized mission-control dashboard where users can monitor ten health and wellness parameters, including heart rate, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), blood pressure, body temperature, respiratory rate, activity, sleep, hydration, and stress.

The application uses a simulated telemetry engine to generate continuous astronaut health readings. These readings are stored in an SQLite database and analyzed through interactive charts, historical records, and an AI-powered anomaly detection system. Using Scikit-learn's Isolation Forest algorithm, personalized health baselines, and statistical analysis, the system identifies unusual patterns and generates alerts to highlight potential health concerns.

ASTRA-MED also includes astronaut profile management, mission management, health analytics, medical history, PDF reports, data exports, and configurable system settings.

2. What benefits does it have?

  • Centralized monitoring: Brings astronaut health information and mission activities together in one platform.
  • Early anomaly identification: Helps identify unusual patterns in simulated health readings through machine learning.
  • Data visualization: Makes complex health information easier to understand through interactive charts and analytics.
  • Historical analysis: Allows users to review, compare, and export previous health readings.
  • Automated alerts: Highlights readings that exceed configured reference thresholds.
  • Secure access: Provides administrator and medical officer roles with different permissions and password protection.
  • Mission management: Organizes astronaut profiles, mission assignments, and mission progress.

3. What is the intended impact of the project?

My goal is to demonstrate how artificial intelligence, data analytics, and software engineering can contribute to astronaut health-monitoring systems. Space missions expose astronauts to challenging environmental conditions, making continuous health awareness and reliable information management important.

ASTRA-MED explores how technology can help mission teams organize health data, recognize unusual trends, and make information more accessible. Its intended impact is to provide a foundation for future intelligent space-health monitoring solutions that could eventually incorporate validated real-world sensor data and more advanced predictive analytics.

4. What tools, programming languages, hardware, and software did I use?

Programming language:

  • Python 3.11+

Frameworks and libraries:

  • CustomTkinter — modern desktop graphical interface.
  • NumPy and Pandas — numerical computation and data processing.
  • SciPy — statistical analysis.
  • Scikit-learn — machine learning and Isolation Forest anomaly detection.
  • Matplotlib and Seaborn — interactive data visualization.
  • Joblib — machine learning model persistence.
  • Pillow — image processing and interface assets.
  • ReportLab — PDF medical report generation.
  • OpenPyXL — Excel data export.

Database and storage:

  • SQLite — local database management.
  • CSV and Excel — health data export and reporting.

Development environment and hardware:

  • Python development environment.
  • Windows-compatible desktop/laptop computer.
  • Standard computer hardware; no specialized medical sensors or space equipment are required because the project uses simulated telemetry.

5. How is the project creative and innovative?

The creativity of ASTRA-MED comes from combining multiple technologies into a single astronaut-focused health-monitoring environment.

Instead of creating a basic dashboard, I designed a mission-control inspired interface that integrates live simulated telemetry, ECG visualization, AI-assisted anomaly detection, personalized baselines, historical health analytics, automated alerts, and mission management.

One particularly important feature is the combination of Isolation Forest with individual astronaut health baselines and extreme-deviation rules. This allows the system to identify unusual readings relative to an astronaut's own historical patterns rather than relying exclusively on general thresholds.

I also incorporated NASA-documented in-flight physiological behavior into the simulation model, using documented findings as a reference while treating simulation scaling factors as engineering assumptions.

6. What factors did I consider during development?

During development, I considered several important factors:

  • Astronaut safety: Health-related information should be clearly presented, and unusual readings should be highlighted.
  • Data accuracy and consistency: Simulated readings should follow realistic patterns and remain within defined limits.
  • Individual differences: Each astronaut should have personalized health baselines for anomaly analysis.
  • User experience: The interface should be organized, intuitive, and easy to navigate.
  • Performance: Background telemetry generation should not interrupt the desktop interface.
  • Security: User authentication, password hashing, role-based permissions, and restricted medical-history access should protect sensitive information.
  • Scalability: The modular architecture should make future enhancements and integrations easier.
  • Reliability: Database operations, backups, testing, and error handling should support consistent application behavior.
  • Medical responsibility: AI-generated results must be treated as statistical indicators, not medical diagnoses.

Overall, ASTRA-MED represents my effort to bring artificial intelligence, data science, and modern desktop software development together to explore a meaningful challenge: monitoring and supporting human health beyond Earth.
